fields.name: units
fields.label: Units on the IESCO bill
fields.hint: Units (kWh) for the month, from the bill or from this and last month's meter readings. Winter heater months and summer AC months both push this up.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed in the connection details of the IESCO bill. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates: enter its peak units under Advanced ([[F13|ToU peak hours]]).

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick only if the bill prints the protected category; one heater month over the limit removes it.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.fc_surcharge_per_unit.value|rs2}} per unit (none on lifeline or protected)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for {{data.fpa_latest.fpa_for}} charged on {{data.fpa_latest.label}} bills. {{data.fpa_newest.note}} Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: fpa_units
fields.label: Units in the FPA month
fields.hint: NEPRA charges the FPA on the units of the month it adjusts (the FPA month, usually two months before this bill), not on this month's units. Copy that month's units from the units history on your bill. Blank = this month's units.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

fields.name: peak_units
fields.label: Units in peak hours (ToU)
fields.hint: Only for a sanctioned load of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more: the peak units on your ToU bill. Blank uses our estimate of {{d.tou_peak_share|pct}} of the units.

fields.name: mdi_kw
fields.label: MDI (ToU)
fields.hint: Only for {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more: the maximum demand printed on a ToU bill. The fixed charge is on the higher of half the sanctioned load and the MDI; blank uses half the sanctioned load.

outputs.label: One unit past that limit adds

answer: An IESCO home in Islamabad or Rawalpindi using {{in.units|int}} units in a month as an unprotected consumer on a {{in.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection pays about {{out.total_rs|rs}}: {{out.energy_rs|rs}} energy charge at {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit, plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the {{data.fpa_latest.fpa_for}} FPA and GST. IESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges, then GST on the subtotal.
how: Energy ({{out.category}}): {{out.energy_calc}} = {{out.energy_rs|rs}}. Fixed charge {{out.fixed_basis}} = {{out.fixed_rs|rs}}. FC surcharge {{out.fc_rs|rs}} + QTA {{out.qta_rs|rs}} + FPA {{out.fpa_rs|rs}}. Subtotal {{out.subtotal_rs|rs}} + GST {{out.gst_pct}}% ({{out.gst_rs|rs}}) = {{out.total_rs|rs}}.
key_facts: IESCO, the Islamabad Electric Supply Company, bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026 across Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal and Jhelum, so {{out.units|int}} units cost the same in Rawalpindi as in Lahore apart from the monthly FPA line.
An unprotected IESCO consumer using {{out.units|int}} units pays {{out.rate|rs2}} on every unit, which is {{out.energy_rs|rs}} of energy charge before the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST.

A heater month of {{ex.1.out.units|int}} units in an Islamabad winter costs about {{ex.1.out.total_rs|rs}} unprotected, while the same home stays at about {{ex.0.out.total_rs|rs}} in a protected month of {{ex.0.out.units|int}} units.

Protection on IESCO needs every one of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} bills at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units on a connection below {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW; one winter month over the limit moves every later bill to unprotected rates until the run is rebuilt.

GST at {{out.gst_pct|int}}% is charged on the energy charge, fixed charge and surcharges together and adds {{out.gst_rs|rs}} to a {{out.units|int}} unit IESCO bill; the surcharge and GST defaults are secondary-source figures that change.

The bill jumps at {{out.cliff_units|int}} units: up to there every unit is billed at {{data.tariff.unprotected.6.rate|rs2}}, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of {{data.tariff.unprotected.7.rate|rs2}}, which adds {{out.cliff_rs|rs}} to the bill of an unprotected {{out.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% on a monthly bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more; consumers on the list pay none.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the IESCO bill

sections.h2: What is the IESCO per unit rate in 2026?
p: IESCO does not set its own rate. It supplies Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal and Jhelum, with some feeders into Azad Kashmir, and bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026. An unprotected home pays the rate of the slab its monthly units reach on every unit: {{out.units|int}} units are all billed at {{out.rate|rs2}}. The lowest slab is the cheapest and the open-ended top slab is the dearest.

Protected and lifeline consumers have their own low rates, worked out slab by slab. The table below prints the rate for each slab from the tariff file, and the worked examples show a protected month, a winter heater month and a summer AC month.

sections.h2: Why is the winter IESCO bill as high as the summer one?
p: Islamabad and Rawalpindi have real winters, and when gas pressure drops many homes switch to electric heating. A fan heater draws about {{a.room-heater-fan.running_w|int}} W and a storage geyser about {{a.electric-geyser-storage.running_w|int}} W, so a few hours a day of each adds hundreds of units to the month. That is how a home that was protected in autumn lands at {{ex.1.out.units|int}} units and a bill of {{ex.1.out.total_rs|rs}} in January.

Summer in the capital region is milder than south Punjab, but an inverter AC still adds a few hundred units. The [[E5|AC units calculator]] estimates the units for your tonnage and hours; this page then turns those units into the IESCO bill.

sections.h2: IESCO bill check: estimate here, confirm on the IESCO site
p: This IESCO bill estimate works from the units you type. The official bill, with the reference number, due date, arrears and the exact FPA, is on the IESCO website, which links the duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number from the top of any earlier bill there. Use this calculator to understand what each printed line should be, to plan next month, or to check a high bill against the slab it should fall in.

If the reading dates on the bill cover more than a month, the units may have been pushed into a higher slab by the long cycle; the [[N1|bill audit tool]] checks that for you. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see [[F14|what the FPA line on your bill means]]. A home on a time-of-use meter can check the [[F13|peak hours for IESCO]].

mistakes: Searching for a separate IESCO tariff. IESCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic slabs; the FPA that moves month to month is one national figure for every DISCO.

Planning the winter on the autumn bill. A heater and a geyser can double the units in January, and one month over {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units ends protected status for the next {{d.protected_months|int}} bills.
Reading the reference number wrong on the duplicate bill page. Type the digits only, without the spaces or dashes some bills print between groups.
Dividing the bill total by units to find the IESCO per unit rate. Fixed charge, surcharges and GST are inside the total; the slab rate is the energy line divided by units.

faq.q: How do I get an IESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and replace the pre-filled FPA with the one on your bill under advanced settings. For {{out.units|int}} units the estimate is {{out.total_rs|rs}}, FPA included.

faq.q: What is the IESCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab the month reaches: {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit for an unprotected home using {{out.units|int}} units. The table above lists the rate for every slab; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: What is the IESCO tariff for 2026?
faq.a: The uniform A-1 domestic tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: lifeline slabs up to {{data.tariff.lifeline.1.upto|int}} units, protected slabs up to {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units, unprotected slabs of {{data.tariff.unprotected.0.upto|int}} units each up to {{data.tariff.unprotected.6.upto|int}} and an open-ended top slab. Connections of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW and above are billed on ToU rates.

faq.q: How do I check my IESCO bill online?
faq.a: The IESCO website links a duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number printed at the top of an earlier bill to see the current bill and its due date. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

The federal capital Islamabad and the districts of Rawalpindi, Attock, Chakwal and Jhelum, with some feeders serving Azad Kashmir. If your bill carries another company's name, use that company's calculator; the slab rates and the FPA are the same, but the official bill and reference number come from that company.

faq.q: Does an electric heater make an IESCO home unprotected?
faq.a: It can. Protection needs all of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} bills at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units. A fan heater of about {{a.room-heater-fan.running_w|int}} W run a few hours a day adds well over a hundred units a month, which is enough to cross the limit.

faq.q: Why does my IESCO bill differ from this estimate?
faq.a: The estimate uses the pre-filled FPA unless you enter your bill's, and it cannot see arrears, late payment surcharge, meter rent or a long reading cycle. Copy the FPA rate from the bill, and if the reading dates cover more than a month, run the bill audit tool.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}}?
faq.a: Usually because of advance income tax, which this estimate leaves out: a domestic consumer not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% on a monthly bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more. [[F1|Who pays the income tax line]] is explained with the electricity bill calculator.
